services.title: Liability Policy and Filing
services.summary: The standard filing after a DWI or suspension.
services.text: The standard Texas filing after a DWI, a suspension or driving without insurance. We quote a policy that clears the state's 30/60/25 limits and file your SR-22 with the DPS.
services.lead: An SR-22 is not a stand-alone policy. It is a certificate of financial responsibility that your insurer transmits to the Texas Department of Public Safety, confirming your liability coverage clears what state law demands.

covers.title: Owner and non-owner filings
covers.text: Filed on an auto policy if you own or regularly drive a car, or as a non-owner's policy if you do not.

covers.title: The 30/60/25 coverage floor
covers.text: $30,000 bodily injury per person, $60,000 per accident and $25,000 property damage. Nothing below those figures holds up the filing.

covers.title: Electronic filing with the DPS
covers.text: The carrier transmits the form directly, which puts the certificate on record the same day your policy activates. There is no mailed-form delay.

covers.title: We confirm the state received it
covers.text: We follow up with the DPS to confirm the filing landed, so you are never left guessing.

covers.title: Renewals tracked
covers.text: We track the term alongside you and warn you before a payment is due, because a lapse can restart the two years.

questions.q: Is an SR-22 a separate insurance policy?
questions.a: No. It is a certificate of financial responsibility your insurer files with the state to prove you carry at least the required coverage. You keep one auto policy, and the SR-22 rides on top of it as proof.

questions.q: How long does Texas require an SR-22?
questions.a: Texas generally holds the filing open for a two-year period, counted from your conviction, crash or judgment date rather than the day you get reinstated. Only unbroken coverage counts toward that stretch.

questions.q: Can I file the certificate myself?
questions.a: No. State law bars self-filing, so an admitted insurer has to submit the certificate. We manage that filing from your first quote until the DPS confirms it is on file.

questions.q: Can I switch insurers while I have an SR-22?
questions.a: Yes, but never cancel the old policy before we file the new SR-22, or the state sees a gap in your coverage. We line up the timing so your filing stays continuous.

services.title: Non-Owner Coverage
services.summary: Meets the requirement with no car of your own.
services.text: No car of your own but you need to reinstate? Texas files a non-owner SR-22 as a non-owner's policy, usually at a lower cost than a standard auto policy.
services.lead: A non-owner SR-22 is the option Texas gives drivers who don't own a car. It supplies the liability coverage state law demands whenever you drive a vehicle that isn't yours: borrowed, rented, or booked through a rideshare app.
services.imageAlt: A driver on an open highway in a car that is not their own

covers.title: No vehicle needed
covers.text: The policy follows you rather than a registered car, so the requirement keeps ticking even when nothing is registered in your name.

covers.title: The same 30/60/25 limits
covers.text: Filed this way, the certificate carries the identical limits an owner policy would, and the DPS treats it as equally valid proof.

covers.title: Borrowed and rented cars
covers.text: It covers you in vehicles that are not yours, including a car booked through a rideshare app.

covers.title: Usually costs less
covers.text: A non-owner filing generally costs less than insuring a vehicle of your own, so we check whether it fits before quoting an owner policy.

questions.q: Can I get an SR-22 in Texas without owning a car?
questions.a: Yes. Texas will file a non-owner SR-22 through the Department of Public Safety as a non-owner's policy, carrying the same 30/60/25 limits an owner policy would.

questions.q: Does it cover a borrowed or rented car?
questions.a: Yes. It supplies the liability coverage state law demands whenever you drive a vehicle that isn't yours, borrowed, rented or booked through a rideshare app.

questions.q: Does it pay to repair the car I borrowed?
questions.a: No. It covers your liability when you drive a vehicle that is not yours, but damage to that car stays with the owner's policy. Ask us which vehicles the state counts as non-owned.

questions.q: What happens when I buy a car?
questions.a: Tell us first. We quote the right owner coverage and move the filing across, so the certificate stays continuous through the change.

covers.title: The SR-22 filed with it

covers.title: No judgment

covers.title: Low down-payment options
covers.text: Needing an SR-22 already makes insurance more expensive, so we look for coverage that satisfies the requirement without costing more than your situation calls for.

questions.q: Is DUI insurance a separate type of policy?
questions.a: No. It is an ordinary auto policy priced for a high-risk record, with the state filing attached to it. The trigger is the violation, not the filing itself.

questions.q: Will an SR-22 show up on a background check?
questions.a: No. An SR-22 is part of your state driving record, not a criminal record. It lives with your motor-vehicle file, separate from anything a criminal search would return.

questions.q: When does the filing end after a DWI?
questions.a: Texas generally holds it open for two years from the conviction, crash or judgment date. A fresh no-insurance conviction can invalidate the filing and restart that term from scratch.

services.title: Suspended License Insurance
services.text: Insurance is one line on the state's reinstatement checklist. We quote the qualifying policy and file the SR-22 that proves financial responsibility.
services.lead: A license suspension usually comes with an insurance requirement attached. Our part is quoting the qualifying policy, filing the certificate against your specific requirement, and confirming with the state that it arrived.

covers.title: Proof of financial responsibility
covers.text: The SR-22 is what certifies to the DPS that your liability coverage clears the state's required limits.

covers.title: Filed the same day

covers.title: The reinstatement fee is separate

covers.title: Coverage that prevents a re-suspension
covers.text: Cancel the policy and the insurer must notify the DPS, putting your license right back under suspension. We track the term so that does not happen.

questions.q: Can insurance alone reinstate a suspended license?
questions.a: No. The Department of Public Safety holds sole authority to reinstate your license. Filing the certificate satisfies the insurance side of the process.

questions.q: How fast can you file my SR-22?
questions.a: The certificate goes to the DPS the same day your policy activates, once eligible coverage is issued and the required information and payment have been received.

questions.q: Will a coverage lapse affect my filing?
questions.a: Yes. A lapse means the insurer files an SR-26 cancellation notice and the DPS suspends your license, and the two-year term can start over.

services.title: Filing Removal
services.summary: Ending the filing on schedule, not early.
services.text: Removal is the state's decision, not ours. We confirm your requirement end date before anything is cancelled, so an early move does not restart the clock.
services.lead: An SR-22 comes off when the state says the requirement is complete. The risk is cancelling early: the insurer files an SR-26, the DPS suspends your license again, and in Texas the two-year period can start over.

covers.title: Your requirement end date
covers.text: The term runs from the conviction, crash or judgment date rather than the day you reinstated, so the two dates are rarely the same.

covers.title: The SR-26 that closes it
covers.text: Once the filing period ends and the state no longer needs your coverage certified, an SR-26 cancellation notice closes it out.

covers.title: Confirmed before you cancel
covers.text: We confirm the date with the state before anything is cancelled. Tell us before you change or cancel anything.

covers.title: Continuous coverage to the finish
covers.text: Only unbroken coverage counts toward the term, which is why keeping the policy paid and active protects your progress.

questions.q: Who ends my SR-22 filing, you or the state?
questions.a: The state. We file your SR-22 and we confirm the end date, but only the Department of Public Safety can decide the requirement is complete.

questions.q: Can a lapse restart my filing period?
questions.a: Yes. A lapse, or a fresh no-insurance conviction, can invalidate the filing outright, and the two years start over from that point.

questions.q: Should I cancel coverage on my removal date?
questions.a: Talk to us first. Cancelling before the state has released the requirement puts your license straight back under suspension.

about.title: Making SR-22 insurance simpler when you need it most.
text: Most people never plan to need an SR-22. It usually enters the picture when something has already gone wrong: a suspended license, a DWI, driving without required insurance, or another event that changes what the state requires from you. Then comes a second problem: figuring out what to do next.

SR-22 Insurance Partners of Texas exists to make that process simpler. We help drivers secure an SR-22 certificate after license suspensions, DUI-related violations and other situations that require proof of financial responsibility, and we assist with standard SR-22 policies, non-owner SR-22 insurance, license reinstatement coverage and SR-22 removal guidance.

Our goal is simple: don't pay more than you need to. Insurance companies evaluate high-risk drivers differently, so one carrier's price can be very different from another's. Our team is available 24 hours a day to answer questions, explain filing requirements and help Texas drivers complete the SR-22 process with less confusion.

faqs.q: How long does Texas require an SR-22?
faqs.a: Texas generally holds the filing open for a two-year period, counted from your conviction, crash or judgment date rather than the day you get reinstated. Only unbroken coverage counts toward that stretch, and a new no-insurance conviction can restart it from zero.

faqs.q: How much does an SR-22 cost in Texas?
faqs.a: The filing itself adds little next to the cost of the policy behind it. Texas separately charges a reinstatement fee that the Department of Public Safety sets and collects on its own, apart from your premium, so it won't show up in your quote.

faqs.q: Can I get an SR-22 in Texas without owning a car?
faqs.a: Yes. Texas will file a non-owner SR-22 through the Department of Public Safety as a non-owner's policy, carrying the same 30/60/25 limits an owner policy would. It keeps the filing active even during stretches when no car is registered in your name.

faqs.q: What happens if my SR-22 lapses in Texas?
faqs.a: A lapse means the insurer files an SR-26 cancellation notice and the Department of Public Safety suspends your license. In Texas a new no-insurance conviction can also invalidate the filing and restart the term from scratch. Tell us before you change or cancel anything.

faqs.q: Will filing an SR-22 automatically reinstate my license?
faqs.a: No. Filing the required certificate can satisfy the insurance portion of the reinstatement process, but only the Department of Public Safety or the court can determine whether all of your reinstatement requirements have been met.

faqs.q: Do I need to have everything ready before I call?
faqs.a: No. Start with why you were told you need an SR-22 and whether you own a vehicle. We can tell you what other information is needed from there.

faqs.q: Can I call even if I'm only comparing prices?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us what you need and we'll help you understand your available insurance options. You're not obligated to purchase a policy just because you requested a quote.

Most orders call for the standard SR-22, and an SR-26 closes it out at the end. The SR-22A applies to a narrower case: it rides alongside an SR-22 after a security deposit tied to a crash or a default judgment, and it locks in a six-month prepaid policy so coverage can't lapse partway through the term.

facts.heading: Texas minimum liability limits
facts.text: An SR-22 is proof your policy clears 30/60/25: $30,000 bodily injury per person, $60,000 per accident and $25,000 property damage. The DPS turns a certificate back for underinsuring more often than for anything else, so we never quote short. Going above the minimum costs little extra and satisfies the DPS exactly the same way.

facts.heading: Filing term
facts.text: The DPS generally holds the filing open for two years, counted from the conviction, crash or judgment date rather than the day you reinstate. Coverage must run unbroken for that stretch to count.

facts.heading: Words you may see on your notice
items: DWI, the Texas term for impaired driving, treated much like a DUI elsewhere
Driving without insurance, operating a vehicle without the liability coverage the state requires
License suspension, a temporary withdrawal of driving privileges until the conditions are satisfied
Ignition interlock device, a breath-test lock a court may order after an impaired-driving offense
